newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to Egypt on Washington summit.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to Egypt on Washington summit.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Monday left Gaza for Egypt where he will try to persuade President Hosni Mubarak to join a Washington summit to end violence between Israel and the Palestinians, witnesses said.

Israel agreed to President Bill Clinton's call on Sunday for a summit with Arab leaders in Washington on the violence -- sparked by Israel's policies in Jerusalem -- in which 55 Palestinians and 14 Israelis have been killed.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told CBS television that Mubarak wanted some assurance that Israel would honour its past agreements with the Palestinians before agreeing to attend the summit that is to include Jordan's King Hussein.

Clinton telephoned Arafat on Sunday to invite him to the talks but the Palestinian president withheld his agreement to attend, a PLO official said, pending Mubarak's participation. U.S. officials said they expected Arafat to attend.
Egyptian Information Minister Safwat el-Sharif told Egypt's state television on Sunday that Israeli President Ezer Weizman also called Mubarak to urge him to attend the summit.

Israel Radio said top PLO official Mahmoud Abbas, also known as Abu Mazen, met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political adviser Dore Gold to discuss the summit's agenda. There was no immediate confirmation of the report by either side.

Netanyahu, who leaves for Washington on Monday afternoon, has said he has no plans to close the controversial Jerusalem tunnel that touched off clashes between protesters and Israeli troops and gunbattles between Israeli and Palestinian forces last week.

Israel's opening of the tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Arab East Jerusalem, whose final status is a matter of hot dispute between Israelis and Arabs, combined with festering Palestinian frustration over Netanyahu's policies to ignite the gun battles.
U.S. officials said the summit was tentatively scheduled to take place on Tuesday and Wednesday.
